rationale: #942 (swift lane, second corpus, full extent 98-file alamofire draw): SW-B converts enum-cased member calls (`Path.method(.get)`) into `instantiates` and retires the dangling `calls`. The retirement removed "the FIRST calls edge with this (source, leaf)" — and `emittedCalls` had already folded both call sites into ONE relationship, so a DIFFERENT site's genuine call vanished. Measured on Tests/TestHelpers.swift: `static var get: Endpoint { method(.get) }` lost its real call to `Endpoint.method` because a property initializer elsewhere in the same type called `Path.method(.get)`; both sites attribute to the enclosing TYPE, so they collide on (source, leaf). The retirement now counts SITES (`callSiteCounts`) and drops the edge only when no genuine site remains — and every site that can emit a `calls` edge is counted, including the BARE identifier calls this fixture's second site is. Both halves are pinned: the construction still converts (instantiates, not calls) and the real call SURVIVES beside it.

expectRelationships.note: `var path = Path.method(.get)` — the enum-cased navigation is construction, and its line is ITS site (22)

#942: the SECOND site (`return method(.get)` inside `static var get`, line 29) is a genuine bare call to `Endpoint.method` and must survive the construction's retirement — pre-fix it was spliced away because the retirement took the first (source, leaf) edge and the bare site never joined the site count. M59.A7: the edge's line must ALSO move to the surviving site — the dedupe kept site 1's edge, whose line (22) belongs to the construction
